[PARAGRAPH] The tenant, a renter or lessee, pays the landlord for the right to use the commercial property exclusively for business purposes during the lease period.
[HEADING-H2] Which types of properties are considered commercial in Singapore?

[PARAGRAPH] Simply put, the contract helps avoid any misunderstanding between the two parties.

[HEADING-H2] Seize the debtor’s assets: The creditor’s powerful remedy of attachment
[PARAGRAPH] When a debtor fails to repay a debt owed to a creditor, the creditor has powerful legal remedies. One of the most effective remedies is known as “attachment”. Attachment is a legal process that allows a creditor to seize assets belonging to the debtor to satisfy the unpaid debt. This article will provide an overview of how attachment works and why it can be a potent tool for creditors seeking repayment.
[HEADING-H3] What is attachment?
[PARAGRAPH] Attachment is a pre-judgement legal remedy that allows a creditor to seize specified assets belonging to the debtor. The purpose is to hold those assets as security until a court judgment can be obtained. If the creditor is awarded a judgment against the debtor, the attached assets can then be sold to satisfy the judgment. Attachment prevents the debtor from hiding or liquidating assets while the legal process unfolds.
[PARAGRAPH] The attachment remedy is authorized by state law. Rules and procedures vary somewhat from state to state. However, there are some common steps:
[PARAGRAPH] – The creditor first files a court petition requesting the right to attach assets belonging to the debtor. This requires showing evidence of the outstanding debt owed.
[PARAGRAPH] – If the petition is approved, the court issues a writ of attachment ordering the seizure of assets. This specifies what can be seized and is served on the debtor.
[PARAGRAPH] – A law enforcement officer or private process server carries out the actual seizure of assets. These may include bank accounts, real estate, vehicles, business assets, and personal property.
[PARAGRAPH] – The debtor has the right to contest the attachment and request a hearing. If they fail to do so promptly, the attachment proceeds.
[HEADING-H3] Why is attachment a powerful remedy?
[PARAGRAPH] There are several reasons why the attachment process heavily favours creditors:
[PARAGRAPH] – It happens quickly before the debtor is aware or has time to hide assets. Elements of surprise and timing are critical.
[PARAGRAPH] – Debtors bear the burden of challenging an attachment and overturning it. This requires time and legal expenses.
[PARAGRAPH] – Courts tend to issue writs of attachment fairly easily. The debtor’s assets remain seized unless they successfully fight the attachment.
[PARAGRAPH] – Attached assets can be sold off relatively quickly if the creditor is awarded a judgment. This converts assets to cash to repay the debt.
[PARAGRAPH] Attachment is a powerful pre-judgement remedy allowing creditors to seize a debtor’s assets to secure debt repayment. While specific rules vary, the element of surprise works heavily in the creditor’s favour. Debtors face an uphill battle to regain control of assets seized via a writ of attachment. This makes attachment a potent tool for creditors seeking repayment.

[HEADING-H2] The vendor’s guide to navigating real estate sales with or without an agent
[PARAGRAPH] The decision to sell your home can be an exciting yet overwhelming process. Do you need an agent or can you sell it yourself? This guide will walk you through the pros and cons of selling with or without an agent so you can make the best decision for your needs.
[HEADING-H3] Working with a real estate agent
[PARAGRAPH] The main benefit of working with a real estate agent is tapping into their extensive knowledge and resources. An experienced agent knows the local housing market inside and out, has access to listings before they go public, and can provide accurate pricing guidance. Here are some other key advantages of working with an agent:
[LIST-ITEM] Marketing expertise – Agents have the skills and tools to market your home effectively online and offline to reach qualified buyers.
[LIST-ITEM] Negotiation skills – Agents serve as a buffer during negotiations and can advocate on your behalf using their negotiation tactics.
[LIST-ITEM] Paperwork knowledge – Real estate transactions require a lot of paperwork that agents are experienced in dealing with.
[LIST-ITEM] Access to MLS – The multiple listing service provides critical data that agents use to price and market your home.
[LIST-ITEM] Expanded reach – Your agent markets your home to their network of contacts plus new prospects.
[PARAGRAPH] The main downside of using an agent is paying their commission, which is typically 5-6% of the home’s sale price. Overall, a skilled agent earns their commission by guiding you through the entire sales process.
[HEADING-H3] Selling your home as the owner
[PARAGRAPH] With the right preparation, you may choose to sell your home yourself without an agent. Here are some key tips for DIY selling:
[LIST-ITEM] Price it right – Research recent comparable sales and get an appraisal to set an accurate asking price. The price is too high and your home could sit.
[LIST-ITEM] Prepare your home – Make any necessary repairs and style updates to maximize your home’s appeal.
[LIST-ITEM] Utilize MLS – Pay to list your home on the MLS so it’s accessible to buyers and agents.
[LIST-ITEM] Market your home – Create print and online ads, hold open houses, and network with contacts.
[LIST-ITEM] Handle paperwork – Familiarize yourself with all required forms and disclosures. Consider legal help.
[LIST-ITEM] Negotiate offers – Be prepared to negotiate fairly but firmly with buyers. Don’t take lowballs.
[PARAGRAPH] The main advantage of selling solo is avoiding the agent commission. However, you take on all the work and responsibility yourself. Only sell alone if you have ample time and energy.
[HEADING-H3] Choose the Best Path For You
[PARAGRAPH] Deciding whether to enlist an agent or go solo depends on your specific situation. Ask yourself if you need help with pricing, marketing, negotiations and paperwork. An agent brings experience and resources that can make the process smoother. But if you’re willing to put in the work, and have a strong network and ample time, you may successfully sell on your own. Analyze the pros and cons to determine the best approach for your sale.

[HEADING-H2] What is Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM)?
[PARAGRAPH] The Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) is a fundamental concept in finance, widely used to determine the expected return on an investment. In the context of Singapore’s vibrant real estate market, CAPM plays a pivotal role in guiding investors to make informed decisions.
[HEADING-H2] Understanding the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM)
[PARAGRAPH] CAPM is a model that describes the relationship between the expected return of an asset and its risk, as measured by beta.
[PARAGRAPH] The formula for CAPM is:
[PARAGRAPH] Expected Return = Risk-Free Rate + β( Market Return − Risk-Free Rate ) Expected Return=Risk-Free Rate+β(Market Return−Risk-Free Rate)
[PARAGRAPH] Where:
[LIST-ITEM] Risk-Free Rate is the return on a risk-free asset, such as a government bond.
[LIST-ITEM] Beta (β) measures the asset’s volatility compared to the overall market.
[LIST-ITEM] Market Return is the expected return of the market.
[PARAGRAPH] In real estate, CAPM can be applied to calculate the expected return on a property investment, considering its risk relative to the overall property market.
[HEADING-H2] Importance of CAPM in real estate and property
[PARAGRAPH] In Singapore’s real estate landscape, CAPM offers several key insights:
[LIST-ITEM] Risk assessment: By understanding the beta of a property or real estate portfolio, investors can gauge its volatility compared to the broader market.
[LIST-ITEM] Return expectations: CAPM helps investors set realistic return expectations based on an asset’s risk profile and prevailing market conditions.
[LIST-ITEM] Portfolio diversification: Using CAPM, investors can assess how different real estate assets might impact the overall risk and return of their portfolios.
[LIST-ITEM] Strategic decision-making: CAPM provides a framework for comparing the risk-adjusted returns of various investment opportunities, aiding in strategic decision-making.
[HEADING-H3] Conclusion
[PARAGRAPH] As with all investment strategies, consulting with financial and real estate professionals can offer a more comprehensive perspective.

[HEADING-H2] What is income tax relief?

[LIST-ITEM] CPF Relief for Self-Employed

[HEADING-H2] What is Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)?
[PARAGRAPH] The Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) is a home loan limit implemented by MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore) that applies to public and private properties.
[PARAGRAPH] The TDSR establishes boundaries on the maximum borrowing capacity for homebuyers. It is currently set at 55% (as of 16 Dec 2021) of their gross monthly income. The primary objective is to promote responsible borrowing among households and enhance the credit evaluation standards of financial institutions.
[PARAGRAPH] It’s important to note that the TDSR is a permanent requirement that all banks and financial institutions must adhere to when assessing various types of loans, including housing loans, refinancing of housing loans, and loans secured by property.
[HEADING-H2] What does the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) do?
[PARAGRAPH] The implementation of the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) is essential for various reasons, as follows:
[PARAGRAPH] The TDSR promotes higher standards in credit evaluation by financial institutions. It encourages lenders to adopt more thorough assessment practices, reducing the lending risk to borrowers struggling to meet their repayment obligations.
[PARAGRAPH] The TDSR acts as a safeguard to prevent borrowers from becoming overly indebted. It promotes financial prudence by encouraging individuals to consider their financial capabilities and make responsible decisions when taking on property loans.
[PARAGRAPH] By preventing borrowers from becoming over-leveraged, the TDSR contributes to the long-term stability of the property market. It helps prevent speculative behaviour and excessive borrowing, reducing the likelihood of market volatility and potential financial crises.
[HEADING-H2] How to calculate Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR)?
[PARAGRAPH] You can use the following formula to calculate your TDSR:
[PARAGRAPH] (Total monthly debt obligations of the borrower / Gross monthly income of the borrower) x 100%
[PARAGRAPH] The numerator of the TDSR formula represents the borrower’s monthly debt obligations, which include various types of outstanding debts, such as property loans (including the loan being applied for), car loans, student loans, renovation loans, and so on.

[PARAGRAPH] The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) system in Singapore is a unique mechanism designed to manage the number of vehicles on the road. Given Singapore’s limited land space, this system helps control traffic congestion by regulating the number of new vehicles that can be registered each year. Here’s a detailed look at how the COE system works, including the basics, the bidding process, and how to renew your COE.
[HEADING-H2] Basics of the COE System
[LIST-ITEM] The COE is essentially a license that allows you to own and use a vehicle in Singapore for 10 years. After this period, you either need to deregister your vehicle or renew the COE to continue using the vehicle.

[LIST-ITEM] Category B: For cars above 1,600cc or 130bhp.
[LIST-ITEM] Category C: For goods vehicles and buses.
[LIST-ITEM] Category D: For motorcycles.
[LIST-ITEM] Category E: Open category, which can be used for any vehicle type except motorcycles and is often used for luxury cars.
[LIST-ITEM] The Land Transport Authority (LTA) determines the number of COEs available each month, known as the COE quota. This quota is based on several factors, including vehicle de-registrations and the government’s target vehicle population.
[HEADING-H2] COE Bidding Process
[LIST-ITEM] COE bidding exercises are conducted twice a month, usually on the first and third Monday. The bidding period lasts for three days, from Monday to Wednesday.
[LIST-ITEM] Step 1: Submission of Bids
Bidders, who are often car dealers or individual buyers, submit their bids electronically through the LTA’s online system. Each bid must meet the minimum reserve price set by the LTA.

[LIST-ITEM] Vehicle owners can renew their COE by paying the PQP before the COE expires. You can choose to renew it for 5 or 10 years. COEs can also be transferred to another person, though this is more common with company-owned vehicles.
[HEADING-H2] How to Renew Your COE
[PARAGRAPH] When your COE is nearing its 10-year expiration, you can either deregister your vehicle or renew your COE for another 5 or 10 years. Here’s how you can renew your COE:
[LIST-ITEM] 5-Year Renewal: Suitable if you’re uncertain about keeping the vehicle long-term. After renewing for 5 years, you cannot renew the COE again and must deregister the vehicle.
[LIST-ITEM] 10-Year Renewal: Ideal if you plan to keep your vehicle for a long time. You can continue renewing every 10 years.
[LIST-ITEM] The PQP is the average of the COE prices over the last three months. You can find the latest PQP on the LTA website or through your vehicle dealer.
[LIST-ITEM] Payments are typically made online through the LTA’s One Motoring portal. Ensure you renew before your COE expires to avoid penalties or losing your vehicle.
[LIST-ITEM] Once payment is complete, your COE will be renewed for the chosen period, all done online without needing to visit any office.
